questions.stem: History is best described as the study of
options: past events of human beings in an orderly way
future events that people expect to happen
the movement of the planets and the stars
plants and animals in their natural homes
questions.explanation: History studies what people did in the past, arranged in the order in which it happened.

questions.stem: Which of these makes History different from ordinary storytelling?
options: History is always told by elders at night
History is based on facts and placed in time
History uses only songs, drums and dances
History is mainly for entertaining children
questions.explanation: History deals with facts and dates; a story may be invented only to entertain.

questions.stem: A person who studies and writes about past events in a careful, organised way is called a
questions.explanation: A historian collects evidence about the past and writes it down in an orderly way.

questions.stem: Chiamaka's grandmother told her a tale about a tortoise that tricked all the birds at a feast in the sky. This tale is NOT History mainly because it
options: is too short to be written down
was told in the Igbo language
has more than one character in it
is not based on real events
questions.explanation: History must be about real events that can be supported by evidence.

questions.stem: Which statement best shows that History is time-based?
options: Events are told only by elderly people at night
Events are always written down in English
Events are arranged in the order in which they took place
Events are chosen because they are interesting
questions.explanation: Chronology, arranging events by time, is a key feature of History.

questions.stem: The word "chronology" in History refers to
options: arranging events in the order of time
the study of rocks and soils of an area
the art of telling folk tales to children
a list of the names of famous kings
questions.explanation: Chronology means placing events in the order of time.

questions.stem: Sources of History are best described as
options: the places where historians build their homes
the rivers that flow through a kingdom
the rules used to govern a town
the means by which we learn about the past
questions.explanation: Sources are where historical information comes from.

questions.stem: Sources of History are usually grouped into
options: oral, written and electronic sources only
ancient, medieval and modern sources only
questions.explanation: The syllabus groups sources as primary, secondary and tertiary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary source of History?
options: Oral tradition told by an elder
questions.explanation: Oral traditions come directly from people close to the events, so they are primary sources.

questions.stem: An old bronze head dug up at an ancient site is an example of
questions.explanation: Objects made and used by people in the past are called artefacts.

questions.stem: Old letters, reports and records kept in a national archive are known as
questions.explanation: Archives keep original records from the past; they are primary sources.

questions.stem: Which of these is a weakness of oral tradition as a source of History?
options: It can only be understood by trained archaeologists
It is always recited in a foreign language by priests
Details may change as it passes from person to person
It tells us nothing about the people of the past
questions.explanation: Oral tradition depends on memory, so details may change over time.

questions.stem: Legends and folklore are classed as primary sources because they
options: are printed in modern History textbooks
are written by teachers for their students
are kept only in libraries outside Nigeria
come directly from the people by word of mouth
questions.explanation: They are passed down from the people themselves.

questions.stem: A History textbook written by a university lecturer is a
questions.explanation: Textbooks are written from other sources, so they are secondary.

questions.stem: The story of a person's life written by that person is called
questions.explanation: An autobiography is a life story written by the person himself or herself.

questions.stem: Which of these is a secondary source of History?
options: A journal article on the Benin Kingdom
A carved ivory mask from old Benin
An elder's account of a war he fought in
A treaty signed by a king in the 1880s
questions.explanation: Journal articles are written from studying earlier evidence.

questions.stem: A book about the life of Nnamdi Azikiwe written by another author is best described as
options: an autobiography, which is a primary source
a biography, which is a secondary source
a memorandum, which is a tertiary source
an artefact, which is a primary source
questions.explanation: A life story written by someone else is a biography, a secondary source.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tertiary source of History?
options: A student's project on Nigerian independence
The oral account of a village elder
Original colonial reports in an archive
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists students' projects, bulletins and memos as tertiary sources.

questions.stem: Bulletins and memoranda are grouped as
questions.explanation: They summarise information from other sources, so they are tertiary.

questions.topic: How to access sources of History
questions.stem: Which of the following is a place where people can see old objects from Nigeria's past?
questions.explanation: Museums keep and display historical objects.

questions.topic: How to access sources of History
questions.stem: Pupils of a school in Jos went on an excursion to see Nok terracotta works. This trip helped them to
options: write a tertiary source of History
avoid the study of History altogether
learn what will happen in the future
questions.explanation: Excursions to museums and sites let students see sources of History.

questions.topic: How to access sources of History
questions.stem: Cultural festivals help us to learn History because they
options: are held only in foreign countries
are organised and paid for by banks
remove the need for written records
show practices handed down from the past
questions.explanation: Festivals preserve traditions from the past.

questions.topic: How to access sources of History
questions.stem: A student wants to read old newspapers and government gazettes from the 1950s. The best place to find them is
questions.explanation: Archives store old official records and newspapers.

questions.stem: One importance of studying History is that it helps people to
options: grow more food crops on their family farms
questions.explanation: History explains how present society came to be.

questions.stem: How does History promote national unity in Nigeria?
options: It teaches that each group should live apart
It encourages citizens to forget their past
It makes one ethnic group superior to the rest
It shows the shared experiences of Nigerian peoples
questions.explanation: Learning shared history helps Nigerians see what binds them together.

questions.stem: Learning about the mistakes of past leaders can help a nation to
questions.explanation: History teaches lessons from past mistakes.

questions.stem: Which of these best explains why History helps to build patriotism?
options: It forces citizens to travel abroad to study
It removes the need for national symbols
It makes citizens proud of their heritage
It teaches citizens to ignore national events
questions.explanation: Knowing their heritage helps citizens love and serve their country.

questions.stem: History helps an individual to know
options: his or her roots and identity
the price of goods next year
the exact time of the next rainfall
how to cure all known diseases
questions.explanation: History tells people where they came from.

questions.stem: The study of History is mainly concerned with
options: people and their activities in the past
wild animals living in the forest today
the chemical make-up of rain water
the shapes of mountains and valleys
questions.explanation: History is about human activities in the past.

questions.stem: A historian compares an elder's account of a war with a colonial officer's written report on the same war. This is done mainly to
options: make the story longer and more exciting
remove all the dates from the story
check the accuracy of the information
turn the story into a song for children
questions.explanation: Comparing sources helps historians test whether information is accurate.

questions.stem: The Nok culture is famous for its
questions.explanation: Nok people made figures from baked clay called terracotta.

questions.stem: The Nok culture site is located in present-day
questions.explanation: Nok village is in southern Kaduna State.

questions.stem: "Terracotta" means
questions.explanation: Terracotta is clay that has been shaped and fired.

questions.stem: The first Nok terracotta head was found by accident by
questions.explanation: Tin miners digging near Nok uncovered the first terracotta pieces.

questions.stem: Remains of furnaces at Nok sites show that the Nok people practised
questions.explanation: Furnace remains show that the Nok people worked iron.

questions.stem: The Nok culture is significant in Nigerian history because it
options: was the first place Europeans landed in Nigeria
was the capital city of the Sokoto Caliphate
produced the first printed books in West Africa
is one of the earliest iron-working cultures in West Africa
questions.explanation: Nok is one of the oldest known iron-working and art-making cultures in West Africa.

questions.stem: The archaeologist closely linked with the study of the Nok terracottas is
questions.explanation: Bernard Fagg studied and made the Nok finds known.

questions.stem: The Nok terracotta heads often have holes in the eyes, nostrils and ears. A possible reason for these holes is to
options: allow air to escape during firing
hold the figures together with nails
show that the people were blind
make the heads lighter for carrying water
questions.explanation: Holes help hot air escape so the clay does not crack while firing.

questions.stem: Ile-Ife is located in present-day
questions.explanation: Ile-Ife is in Osun State.

questions.stem: Ile-Ife is regarded by the Yoruba as their
questions.explanation: Yoruba traditions describe Ife as the cradle of the Yoruba people.

questions.stem: According to Yoruba tradition, the founder of Ile-Ife was
questions.explanation: Tradition names Oduduwa as the founder of Ife.

questions.stem: The traditional ruler of Ile-Ife is called the
questions.explanation: The Ooni (Oni) is the ruler of Ile-Ife.

questions.stem: The famous Ife heads were made mainly of
questions.explanation: Ife artists produced brass (often called bronze) and terracotta heads.

questions.stem: Ife art is especially admired because its human heads are
options: made only of paper and glue
questions.explanation: Ife heads look like real people; this is called naturalism.

questions.stem: Many Yoruba kingdoms trace their origin to Ife. This shows that Ife was
options: a small fishing village on the coast
a European trading fort on the Atlantic coast
a resting place on a desert trade route
an important political and religious centre
questions.explanation: Many Yoruba rulers claim descent from Ife, showing its importance.

questions.stem: The ancient Benin Kingdom is located in present-day
questions.explanation: Benin City is the capital of Edo State.

questions.stem: The traditional ruler of the Benin Kingdom is called the
questions.explanation: The ruler of Benin is the Oba.

questions.stem: Benin artists were famous for making
questions.explanation: Benin brass plaques and heads show the history of the kingdom.

questions.stem: The Benin brass casters were organised in a
options: guild that worked for the Oba
unit of the colonial police force
questions.explanation: Brass casters formed a guild serving the royal court.

questions.stem: The method used by Benin and Igbo-Ukwu artists to cast metal objects is called
questions.explanation: In lost-wax casting, a wax model is replaced by molten metal.

questions.stem: In 1897, many Benin bronzes were taken to Europe after
options: the Oba sold them to Portuguese traders for guns
a British military expedition against Benin
questions.explanation: British forces attacked Benin in 1897 and carried away many works of art.

questions.stem: The Oba of Benin who was sent into exile in Calabar by the British in 1897 was
questions.explanation: Oba Ovonramwen was exiled to Calabar after the 1897 expedition.

questions.stem: The Benin plaques are important to historians because they
options: show the map of the Sahara Desert
record events at the royal court
are written in the Arabic script
questions.explanation: The plaques show kings, warriors and ceremonies, recording Benin's history.

questions.stem: Igbo-Ukwu is located in present-day
questions.explanation: Igbo-Ukwu is a town in Anambra State.

questions.stem: The Igbo-Ukwu bronzes were first found when
options: a man was digging a cistern in his compound
a road was being built by the British army
a ship sank in the River Niger at Lokoja
tin miners were digging near a hill
questions.explanation: Isaiah Anozie found them while digging a cistern.

questions.stem: The archaeologist who carried out major excavations at Igbo-Ukwu was
questions.explanation: Thurstan Shaw excavated Igbo-Ukwu around 1959–1960.

questions.stem: Which of these was found at Igbo-Ukwu?
options: Terracotta heads found by tin miners
Brass plaques from the Oba's royal palace
Decorated bronze vessels and many beads
questions.explanation: Igbo-Ukwu produced detailed bronze objects and many beads.

questions.stem: The thousands of glass beads found at Igbo-Ukwu suggest that its people
options: learnt glass making from the British
questions.explanation: Many beads were not made locally, pointing to long-distance trade.

questions.stem: Which statement about Igbo-Ukwu bronzes is correct?
options: They were made by Portuguese sailors in Benin
They were carved from large blocks of wood
They are among the oldest bronzes in West Africa
They were discovered in present-day Kaduna State
questions.explanation: Igbo-Ukwu bronzes date to about the ninth or tenth century AD.

questions.stem: A common item among the Igbo-Ukwu finds is
options: a terracotta head of a king
a brass plaque of a soldier
a stone carving of a lion
questions.explanation: The roped pot is one of the best-known Igbo-Ukwu bronzes.

questions.stem: The ancient Ghana Empire was located in
options: the area between the Senegal and Niger rivers
the same place as the modern Republic of Ghana
the forest belt of southern Nigeria
the eastern coast of Africa near Kenya
questions.explanation: Old Ghana lay north-west of modern Ghana, in parts of today's Mali and Mauritania.

questions.stem: The capital of the ancient Ghana Empire was
questions.explanation: Kumbi Saleh was the capital of old Ghana.

questions.stem: The people who founded the ancient Ghana Empire were the
questions.explanation: The Soninke people built the Ghana Empire.

questions.stem: Ancient Ghana became rich mainly through trade in
questions.explanation: Ghana controlled the trade in gold with North African merchants.

questions.stem: One factor that helped the rise of the Ghana Empire was
options: its control of the trans-Saharan trade routes
its large navy on the Atlantic Ocean
questions.explanation: Taxes on trade passing through Ghana made it rich and strong.

questions.stem: The title of the king of ancient Ghana was "Ghana", meaning
questions.explanation: The ruler's title "Ghana" meant war chief, and the empire took the name.

questions.stem: Which of these contributed to the fall of the Ghana Empire?
options: The arrival of the British in 1900
Attacks by the Almoravids from North Africa
questions.explanation: Almoravid attacks in the eleventh century weakened Ghana.

questions.stem: How did the king of Ghana raise money from traders?
options: By selling crude oil to European traders
By printing paper money for the markets
By charging fees at its Atlantic seaports
By taxing goods entering and leaving the empire
questions.explanation: Taxes on salt, gold and other goods filled the royal treasury.

questions.stem: The decline of trade through ancient Ghana was partly caused by
options: the building of railways by the British
a shift of trade routes to other areas
the drying up of the Atlantic Ocean
questions.explanation: When trade routes moved, Ghana lost its main income.

questions.stem: The kingdom that conquered what remained of Ghana before the rise of Mali was
questions.explanation: Sumanguru of Sosso took over Ghana's lands before Sundiata defeated him.

questions.stem: The founder of the Mali Empire was
questions.explanation: Sundiata founded Mali after defeating Sumanguru.

questions.stem: Sundiata Keita defeated Sumanguru at the Battle of
questions.explanation: The Battle of Kirina (about 1235) led to the rise of Mali.

questions.stem: The ruler of Mali famous for his pilgrimage to Mecca with large amounts of gold was
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage made Mali famous for its wealth.

questions.stem: The title "Mansa" used by rulers of Mali means
questions.explanation: Mansa was the title of the Mali rulers.

questions.stem: Timbuktu became famous during the Mali Empire as a centre of
questions.explanation: Timbuktu had mosques and scholars and was a busy trading town.

questions.stem: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca had which effect on Mali?
options: It brought the trans-Saharan trade to an end
It turned Mali into a British colony
It made Mali famous far beyond West Africa
It caused Mali to collapse immediately
questions.explanation: His journey spread news of Mali's riches far beyond West Africa.

questions.stem: One cause of the decline of the Mali Empire was
options: the arrival of steamships on the Niger
decisions taken at the Berlin Conference
weak rulers and quarrels over succession
questions.explanation: Later weak kings and struggles for the throne weakened Mali.

questions.stem: The Moroccan traveller who visited Mali and wrote about it was
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta described Mali after visiting it in the fourteenth century.

questions.stem: The Mali Empire grew rich mainly from
questions.explanation: Mali controlled gold fields and trade routes.

questions.stem: Mali, like Ghana and Songhai, was located in
questions.explanation: The three empires were in the savannah region called the Western Sudan.

questions.stem: The capital of the Songhai Empire was
questions.explanation: Gao on the River Niger was the capital of Songhai.

questions.stem: The Songhai ruler who expanded the empire by conquering Timbuktu and Jenne was
questions.explanation: Sunni Ali built Songhai into a great empire.

questions.stem: Askia Muhammad of Songhai is remembered for
options: abolishing the slave trade in Britain
signing the treaty at the Berlin Conference
questions.explanation: Askia Muhammad organised the empire well and supported scholars.

questions.stem: The Songhai Empire fell after it was defeated by the Moroccans at the Battle of
questions.explanation: The Moroccan army defeated Songhai at Tondibi in 1591.

questions.stem: The Moroccan army defeated Songhai mainly because the Moroccans had
questions.explanation: Guns gave the Moroccans a strong advantage over Songhai spears and arrows.

questions.stem: One factor that helped the rise of Songhai was
options: support from the Royal Niger Company
its position on the Atlantic coast
the discovery of crude oil in Gao
its position along the River Niger
questions.explanation: The River Niger helped Songhai trade and move troops.

questions.stem: Like Ghana and Mali, Songhai depended greatly on
questions.explanation: All three empires grew rich from trade across the Sahara.

questions.stem: Which of these was the largest of the three Western Sudanese empires?
questions.explanation: Songhai covered the largest area of the three.

questions.stem: Which order shows the rise of the Western Sudanese empires from earliest to latest?
questions.explanation: Ghana came first, then Mali, then Songhai.

questions.stem: Internal quarrels among members of the royal family weakened Songhai before the Moroccan invasion. This shows that
questions.explanation: Disputes over the throne made Songhai less able to defend itself.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade

questions.explanation: The trade crossed the Sahara Desert.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
questions.stem: The animal most used for transporting goods across the Sahara was the
questions.explanation: Camels can travel long distances without water.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
questions.stem: Traders crossing the Sahara travelled in large groups called
questions.explanation: A caravan is a group of traders and camels travelling together.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
questions.stem: Trans-Saharan traders stopped at oases mainly to
questions.explanation: Oases have water in the desert.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
questions.stem: Desert guides such as the Tuareg were important to the trans-Saharan trade because they
options: built ships to carry the traders
knew the routes and protected caravans
printed money for use by the traders in markets
produced palm oil for the caravans
questions.explanation: Guides led caravans safely across the desert.

questions.topic: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
questions.stem: A system in which goods are exchanged directly for other goods without money is called
questions.explanation: Much early trade was by exchange of goods.

questions.stem: Which commodity was brought from North Africa to West Africa during the trans-Saharan trade?
questions.explanation: Salt came from the Sahara and North Africa.

questions.stem: Which group of goods was taken from West Africa across the Sahara?
questions.explanation: West Africa sent gold, kola nuts, ivory and slaves north.

questions.stem: Horses were imported into West Africa through the trans-Saharan trade mainly for
options: use by the cavalry in war
carrying palm oil to the coast
questions.explanation: Horses strengthened the armies of Sudanese states.

questions.stem: Salt was highly valued in West Africa during the trans-Saharan trade because
options: it was used to make guns and gunpowder
it was the only form of money in Europe
it grew on trees in the forest belt
it was needed to preserve food and for good health
questions.explanation: People needed salt for diet and to preserve food.

questions.stem: Which of these was a trans-Saharan trade route linking Nigeria with North Africa?
questions.explanation: The Kano–Fezzan route linked Hausaland with North Africa.

questions.stem: The Borno–Tripoli route linked Kanem-Borno with
questions.explanation: Tripoli is on the Mediterranean coast of Libya.

questions.stem: Kano became a major commercial city mainly because it
options: was the first port built by the British
was located on the Atlantic coast
had the first railway line in Africa
lay at the end of important trans-Saharan routes
questions.explanation: Caravans from North Africa ended in Kano, making it a market centre.

questions.stem: One effect of the trans-Saharan trade was the spread of
questions.explanation: Muslim traders spread Islam along the trade routes.

questions.stem: The trans-Saharan trade led to the use of the Arabic language in West Africa for
questions.explanation: Arabic writing was used for records and learning.

questions.stem: Which of these was a negative effect of the trans-Saharan trade?
options: Introduction of new goods to the region
questions.explanation: Captives were taken north and sold as slaves.

questions.stem: The trans-Saharan trade encouraged the growth of which towns?
questions.explanation: These towns became great markets on the desert routes.

questions.stem: The first Europeans to reach the Nigerian coast were the
questions.explanation: Portuguese sailors reached Benin in the fifteenth century.

questions.stem: Early Europeans who came to Nigeria can be grouped as
questions.explanation: These three groups made the first contacts.

questions.stem: The Scottish explorer who travelled on the River Niger and died at Bussa was
questions.explanation: Mungo Park died at the Bussa rapids in 1806.

questions.stem: The Lander brothers are remembered for
options: finding where the River Niger enters the sea
questions.explanation: Richard and John Lander traced the Niger to the Atlantic in 1830.

questions.stem: Christian missionaries contributed to Nigeria mainly by
questions.explanation: Missions set up schools and health centres.

questions.stem: Samuel Ajayi Crowther is remembered as
options: the first African bishop of the Anglican Church
the leader of the Sokoto Jihad
questions.explanation: Crowther, a freed slave, became an Anglican bishop in 1864.

questions.stem: The Scottish missionary who worked in Calabar and fought against the killing of twins was
questions.explanation: Mary Slessor stopped twin killing in Calabar areas.

questions.stem: The trans-Atlantic slave trade involved carrying Africans across the Atlantic Ocean to
questions.explanation: Slaves were taken to work on plantations in the Americas.

questions.stem: Which of these was a major slave port on the Nigerian coast?
questions.explanation: Badagry, Bonny and Calabar were slave ports.

questions.stem: The trans-Atlantic slave trade is often called a triangular trade because
options: it used three kinds of camels in the desert
only three countries took part in the trade
ships moved between Europe, Africa and the Americas
slaves were sold three times in each year
questions.explanation: The route formed a triangle across the Atlantic.

questions.stem: One serious effect of the trans-Atlantic slave trade on Nigeria was
options: a great growth in the population
an end to all wars between states
the rise of Islamic learning centres
questions.explanation: Many strong young people were taken away.

questions.stem: Britain abolished the slave trade in
questions.explanation: The British Parliament passed the abolition law in 1807.

questions.stem: Which of these helped to bring the slave trade to an end?
options: The founding of the Mali Empire in the Sudan
British naval patrols off the West African coast
The discovery of the Nok culture by tin miners
The building of the city wall around Kano
questions.explanation: The British navy stopped slave ships at sea.

questions.stem: "Legitimate trade" refers to trade in
options: slaves shipped across to the Americas
salt carried across the Sahara Desert by camel
weapons sold secretly to rebel groups
goods such as palm oil instead of people
questions.explanation: Legitimate trade replaced the slave trade.

questions.stem: Palm oil was in great demand in Europe in the nineteenth century mainly for
options: building wooden ships for the navy
questions.explanation: Industries in Europe used palm oil for soap and as a lubricant.

questions.stem: The Niger Delta area became known as the "Oil Rivers" because of its
questions.explanation: The name came from the palm oil trade before crude oil was found.

questions.stem: Jaja of Opobo and Nana of Itsekiri were famous during the period of legitimate trade as
questions.explanation: Both controlled trade and were exiled when they resisted British control.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: A centralized state is one in which
options: power is held by a central authority such as a king
every family rules itself without any leader
there is no form of government at all
only foreigners are allowed to make the laws
questions.explanation: In a centralized state, a king or central government holds authority over the whole state.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these was a centralized state in pre-colonial Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Oyo had a king, the Alaafin, ruling over a large empire.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The ruler of the Oyo Empire was called the
questions.explanation: The Alaafin ruled Oyo.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: In the Oyo Empire, the council of kingmakers that checked the power of the Alaafin was the
questions.explanation: The Oyo Mesi, led by the Bashorun, advised and checked the Alaafin.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: In the Oyo political system, the Ogboni society was important because it
options: checked the power of the Oyo Mesi and the Alaafin
commanded the navy of the Oyo Empire
collected tolls on the trans-Saharan routes
ran the mission schools in the capital
questions.explanation: The Ogboni balanced power between the Alaafin and the Oyo Mesi.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The head of the army in the Oyo Empire was the
questions.explanation: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo was the field commander of the Oyo army.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The ruler of Kanem-Borno in its early period was called the
questions.explanation: Kanem-Borno rulers were known as Mai, later Shehu.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The Kanem-Borno ruler who strengthened the empire with firearms and reformed the administration was
questions.explanation: Mai Idris Alooma used muskets and reorganised Borno.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: According to legend, the Hausa states trace their origin to
questions.explanation: The Bayajidda legend explains the origin of the Hausa states.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The ruler of a Hausa state before the jihad was known as the
questions.explanation: Each Hausa state was ruled by a Sarki.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The ruler of the Igala Kingdom is called the
questions.explanation: The Attah of Igala rules from Idah.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The legendary founder of the Nupe Kingdom was
questions.explanation: Tradition says Tsoede (Edegi) founded the Nupe Kingdom.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: In the Niger Delta city states such as Bonny, the basic unit of political and trading organisation was the
questions.explanation: The House system organised trade and government in the city states.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: The secret society that helped to make laws, settle disputes and enforce payment of debts in old Calabar was
questions.explanation: The Ekpe society was powerful in Efik government in Calabar.

questions.topic: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of a centralized state?
options: A clear chain of command from the ruler
No leader of any kind at all in the land
No laws, courts or taxes of any kind
questions.explanation: Centralized states have a ruler and officials at different levels.

questions.stem: A non-centralized (stateless) society is one where
options: one king rules over a very large empire
foreign officers make all the laws
power is shared among elders and family heads
the army controls every part of life
questions.explanation: Authority is spread among many groups instead of one king.

questions.stem: Which of these peoples had a non-centralized system in pre-colonial times?
questions.explanation: Most Igbo communities were governed without a king.

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Igbo society, the symbol of authority held by family heads was the
questions.explanation: The Ofo staff showed the authority of a family head.

questions.stem: In Igbo communities, young men of about the same age who worked together for the community formed
questions.explanation: Age grades did public work and kept order.

questions.stem: The Tiv people of pre-colonial Nigeria are an example of a
questions.explanation: The Tiv were organised by lineages without a central king.

questions.stem: In a typical pre-colonial Igbo village, important decisions were taken by
options: a single king who ruled alone
the village assembly of adult males
the Mai and his council of state
questions.explanation: Igbo democracy allowed open debate at the village assembly.

questions.stem: Which of these is a characteristic of non-centralized states?
options: Decisions are reached by discussion and agreement
A standing army controlled by one ruler
A large system of royal tax collectors
Rule by a powerful hereditary emperor
questions.explanation: Leaders in such societies usually reached agreement by discussion.
